t:
(a) The Secretary shall provide to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate:
        (1) Detailed monthly enrollment figures from the Exchanges established under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act of 2010 pertaining to enrollments during the open enrollment period; and 
        (2) Notification of any new or competitive grant awards, including supplements, authorized under section 330 of the Public Health Service Act.  
    (b) The Committees on Appropriations of the House and Senate must be notified at least 2 business days in advance of any public release of enrollment information or the award of such grants.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that advance notification before a grant award or 'public release' is a consultative step. But the only recipients are the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, which sit inside the federal government, and the 'public release' is a one-way disclosure, not a chance for outside input. The grants mentioned are awards, not participation, so no outside party is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: The Committees on Appropriations of the House and Senate must be notified at least 2 business days in advance of any public release of enrollment information or the award of such grants.

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary to report information and provide notifications to congressional committees. Congress is considered part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress as a form of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall provide to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate: (1) Detailed monthly enrollment figures... and (2) Notification of any new or competitive grant awards...

opus.w: The section only requires the Secretary to send enrollment figures and grant-award notices to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, which are part of Congress and so inside the federal government. It might look like participation because it mentions "public release" and grant awards, but publishing information is not consulting the public, and announcing grants is not an outside party taking part in a decision. No one outside the federal government is consulted.
opus.s: The Secretary shall provide to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary to provide reports and notifications to the Committees on Appropriations of the House and Senate. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this is intra-governmental reporting, not participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: (a) The Secretary shall provide to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate: (1) Detailed monthly enrollment figures... and (2) Notification of any new or competitive grant awards... (b) The Committees on Appropriations of the House and Senate must be notified at least 2 business days in advance of any public release of enrollment information or the award of such grants.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying the Committees on Appropriations constitutes "participation" because it involves external oversight or coordination before a decision (public release or grant award) is finalized. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to or notifying Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
